title: Swamp White Oak: Ancient Swamp White Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: An oak Canada counts as rare. At Gettysburg, General Sickles gathered his officers in one's shade on 2 July 1863, and that tree still stands.
intro: The swamp white oak is rare in Canada, where its population is a tiny fraction of the bur oak's, and we map three of them: one on a battlefield, one in a forest preserve and one in a city where nobody thought the species grew wild. On the afternoon of 2 July 1863, General Daniel Sickles gathered his officers in the shade of the oak at the Trostle Farm in Gettysburg before pushing his corps to the Peach Orchard. The artist Charles Reed sketched the tree that day, and at roughly 175 to 220 years it is still alive. In Spears Woods outside Chicago, Cook County's second-ranked swamp white oak stands 21.9 metres tall under a crown about as wide. And in Ottawa's Dominion Arboretum, the species was not believed native to the region until a few very mature trees turned up near the city.
